tasks.short: Develop breach response and recovery strategies

steps.what: Define breach scenarios, recovery constraints and responsible decision-makers
Draft response and recovery strategies from the agreed scenarios

loop.purpose: Draft response and recovery options within known capabilities
loop.input: Engineer-selected scenarios, constraints, responsibilities and current recovery procedures
loop.output: One draft strategy set with source-linked assumptions and unresolved dependencies
loop.check: Engineer verifies that proposed actions match available capabilities, preserve necessary evidence and have realistic recovery dependencies; a tabletop review challenges the sequence and authority
loop.stop: One draft; invented capabilities, missing recovery evidence or unclear authority return to manual strategy writing, with no operational execution
loop.why_not_simpler: Reuse current plans first; a changed scenario may require a new narrative sequence and trade-off explanation beyond fixed template fields

steps.what: Challenge the strategies with owners and finalise recovery decisions

tasks.design: Adapt existing {DOCS} recovery procedures with one bounded strategy draft. The engineer and responsible owners challenge the assumptions and dependencies; drafting creates neither an executable response nor new incident authority.
tasks.previous_blocker: A changed breach scenario can require substantial first-pass strategy writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-bound drafting can organise supplied constraints into options for review.
tasks.still_hard: Unverified recovery capability and conflicts between containment, evidence and service continuity.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer recognises when a plausible sequence cannot work in the actual environment.
tasks.altitude: Less first-pass writing while response trade-offs remain an accountable discussion.

reach.learn: Connect technical recovery steps to service needs

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a model can draft strategies from selected facts, but recovery feasibility requires independent engineering and owner review.

assumptions: Boundary is developing response strategy, not running an incident or administering backups. Existing owner participation is unchanged.

Engineer captures scenario, affected services, dependencies, existing recovery capability, authority roles and evidence constraints in s1's 40 hours. Service and recovery owners supply the underlying facts as existing work. Missing capability evidence causes manual clarification rather than an inferred recoverable flag.
Try current plans and native templates before a model; existing document runtime earns no saving.
Tabletop observations are produced during the counted review in s3 before finalisation, not assumed to exist beforehand.
unknowns: Time currently spent on first-pass drafting
research_questions: Does a reviewed draft reduce writing time after counting false assumptions and tabletop corrections?

already_counted.description: Owner challenge and final strategy judgement

incremental.description: Source-context upkeep and rejected strategy assumptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=89.5, gross=10.5 and net=5.5 after five upkeep hours. Range assumes useful initial prose; capability validation and strategy decisions retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Preserve and select authorised breach evidence with provenance
Assemble a time-ordered evidence table from specified event fields
Investigate breach causes and vulnerabilities using the original evidence
Evaluate damage and document confirmed impacts and uncertainty

tasks.design: Configure {OTHER} evidence-analysis tools to assemble a traceable event table from engineer-selected fields while preserving originals. The engineer investigates vulnerabilities and evaluates damage in {DOCS}; event order alone establishes neither causation nor the absence of data loss.
tasks.previous_blocker: Investigators may repeatedly copy and sort event records into a timeline.
tasks.enabler_now: Native evidence tools can map known event fields and retain source references.
tasks.still_hard: Clock differences, incomplete evidence and distinguishing access from confirmed impact.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer tests alternative explanations and states what remains unknown.
tasks.altitude: Less timeline assembly while evidence handling, causation and damage judgement remain human.

reach.task: Explain a timeline provenance or clock issue
reach.learn: Preserve original records and separate observation from inference

evidence.claim: Eye Security provides managed detection and response with analysts making decisions; the digest does not establish automatic forensic conclusions.
Model knowledge: a traceable event table can be assembled deterministically from specified fields, but chronology does not prove breach cause or damage.

assumptions: Boundary is investigation and impact assessment, excluding live containment, remediation and statutory reporting.

Existing source systems produce raw events. Engineer preserves originals and captures source ID, record reference, timestamp field, time zone, known clock uncertainty, event field mapping and evidence hashes in s1's 30 hours. Missing timestamps or unsupported formats remain explicit exceptions for manual examination; no structured cause or compromised flag is assumed.
Use native evidence-analysis configuration before custom code; the 25% share requires actual manual copying and sorting, not existing collection runtime.
All source selection and preservation time is retained; no new evidence-collection duty is shifted without cost.
research_questions: Can the generated timeline reproduce source records without concealing time uncertainty or missing evidence?

incremental.description: Mapping upkeep and manual normalisation exceptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75, gross=25 and net=18 after seven upkeep hours. Range assumes partial manual timeline assembly; all substantive investigation and damage evaluation keep their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Choose protection requirements and assess existing security-software capabilities
Develop a candidate software or configuration change for the chosen protection

loop.purpose: Draft residual custom protection code or configuration for review
loop.input: Engineer-selected protection design, interfaces and non-sensitive development context
loop.output: One candidate change in an isolated development branch
loop.check: Engineer verifies intended protection, legitimate allowed behaviour, error handling and secret references, then tests independently against the specified expected outcomes
loop.stop: One candidate; unsupported interfaces, exposed secrets or failed checks return to manual implementation, with no install or production access
loop.why_not_simpler: Configure packaged security functions first; a model is only considered for remaining custom implementation that cannot be expressed by an existing supported template

steps.what: Test the protection candidate in an isolated environment
Approve and install the exact tested protection package
Verify protection and service behaviour after installation

tasks.design: Prefer native {OTHER} security-software configuration before custom development. Where custom implementation remains, draft one candidate and retain engineering review, isolated testing, exact-package installation approval and live verification.
tasks.previous_blocker: A chosen protection design can still require first-pass implementation writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding assistance can supply a candidate that the engineer independently evaluates.
tasks.still_hard: A working build may still allow the wrong access or disrupt legitimate service.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer judges whether the control meets the intended protection goal.
tasks.altitude: Less first-pass development while protection design and production responsibility stay human.

reach.learn: Specify both protected and legitimate behaviours

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot provides code completion and review with expected oversight; this supports candidate implementation rather than validated protection software.
Model knowledge: protection software needs independent tests of both restricted and legitimate behaviour, even when code compiles.

assumptions: Boundary is protection-software implementation and installation, excluding response strategy and separate operational monitoring.

Engineer captures target environment, protection requirements, interfaces, allowed and denied behaviour, managed secret references and independent acceptance examples in s1's 25 hours. Missing requirements stop drafting for manual design; no generated secure flag is accepted.
Test packaged native configuration first; installation-only cases may have no first-draft coding saving. Existing runtime earns no saving.
Private keys and credentials remain in approved stores; candidate drafting has no production access.
research_questions: Does reviewed drafting reduce custom implementation time after counting rejected code and protection regressions?

already_counted.description: Independent tests, approved installation and verification

approvals.approved_version: Exact tested package hash, configuration, target environment, test evidence and rollback version checked in s4; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=89.5, gross=10.5 and net=5.5 after five upkeep hours. Range assumes residual custom implementation; package selection, testing, installation and verification keep their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Oversee plans for file protection and emergency processing

steps.what: Review proposed safeguards and emergency processing plans against organisational needs
Challenge plan owners and coordinate revisions or escalations

tasks.design: Keep oversight of file safeguards and emergency processing with the engineer and plan owners. Plans in {DOCS} are examined for feasibility and coverage; this oversight task does not claim the plan authors' drafting time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Oversight requires challenging whether proposed safeguards meet actual needs.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing plan records support review without replacing the engineering judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Unproven assumptions about backups, access boundaries and emergency dependencies.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer can require evidence and escalate a gap rather than accept reassuring prose.
tasks.altitude: Oversight and escalation responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Translate technical protection gaps into operational implications

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: oversight of safeguard plans depends on evidence, feasibility and accountable discussion with plan owners.

assumptions: Boundary is engineering oversight of plans authored by existing owners, excluding plan drafting, specific breach-strategy work and actual control implementation. Allocate overlap once in the local roll-up.

Existing safeguard and emergency-processing owners produce proposed plans and dependency evidence before s1; their existing work is unchanged and excluded from the focal denominator. Engineer checks them within its 60 hours and captures revisions in s2's 40 hours. Missing evidence causes manual clarification; no adequate-plan flag is presumed.
Use native plan records before adding tools; current runtime earns no saving.
Zero upkeep because no changed oversight process or technology is proposed.
unknowns: Available evidence of recovery and safeguard effectiveness
research_questions: Which plan assumptions cannot currently be supported with operational evidence?

already_counted.description: Substantive plan review and owner challenge

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross and net=0. All oversight judgement remains and no other role's drafting time enters the saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce first-pass strategy or code writing and timeline assembly while retaining engineering judgement over recovery, evidence and protection.
reach: Clarify recovery dependencies with continuity managers
Explain protection acceptance tests to developers
skills_to_grow: Bind installations to exact tested packages
role.ambitious_version: A security engineer who can explain what evidence supports and make traceable protection decisions with less repetitive assembly work.
